title: docs(fields): the auto-number page teaches the spec's format tokens, with no quarter token and no hand-written renderer (objectui#12258)
body:
Fixes #12258

Clause-②: no

The auto-number field page taught a `{Q}` quarter token. `@objectstack/spec`'s `parseAutonumberFormat` has no quarter token: it reads `{Q}` as a `{field_name}` reference to a field called `Q`. This PR removes the token, lists the tokens the spec's parser actually reads, and replaces the page's hand-written generator with the spec's own renderer. Docs only: one file, `content/docs/fields/auto-number.mdx`, with no package touched and no changeset owed (`check-changeset-presence` says so below).

## What changed

- **Mixed Format.** The `format: '{YY}Q{Q}-{000}'` line (commented `24Q1-001`) is gone.
- **Format Placeholders.** The `{Q}` - Quarter (1-4) bullet is gone. The list now names its source, `parseAutonumberFormat` (`@objectstack/spec/data`), and adds the two tokens that parser reads and the list left out:
  - `{YYYYMMDD}`, which the page's own Date-Based example already used.
  - `{field_name}`, because it is how `{Q}` actually gets read.
  - A short paragraph follows. It says the date tokens are exact and case-sensitive, and that there is no quarter, week or time token. It says any other name in braces is a field reference, so `{Q}` reads field `Q`. It also says what happens when that field does not exist or is empty.
- **Backend Implementation.** The hand-written `generateAutoNumber` is gone. It was a `.replace` chain with its own `{Q}` rule, and it had no `{YYYYMMDD}` or field tokens. In its place:
  - ObjectUI does not render the format.
  - An ObjectStack backend mints the value at insert time with `parseAutonumberFormat` and `renderAutonumber` from `@objectstack/spec/data`, the renderer its query engine and SQL driver share.
  - A custom backend should call the same two functions rather than re-implement the grammar.
- **Sequence Management, one paragraph.** This is a bounded in-place repair (section below). The old text said to partition the counter per year "only if the format resets", for when the sequence "is meant to restart each January". It now states the spec's rule: the counter scope is whatever renders before the `{0000}` slot. So `'ORD-{YYYY}-{0000}'` restarts each January, and `'ORD-{0000}'` keeps one count.

## What each claim on the page rests on (measured)

These readings use `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0, the version this workspace installs, imported from `@objectstack/spec/data` with `now` = 2024-03-15:

- **The card's reading, reproduced.** `parseAutonumberFormat('{YY}Q{Q}-{000}')` gives `date YY · literal Q · field Q · literal - · seq 3`. `renderAutonumber` with no record gives `24Q-001`. `missingFieldValues` on that format with an empty record gives `["Q"]`.
- **What an author actually gets: a refusal, not a silently wrong number.** Read in objectstack source at `36b2889cd`:
  - The engine's autonumber path throws `Cannot generate autonumber ... referenced field(s) [Q] are empty on the record`.
  - `lintAutonumberFormats` refuses a `{field}` token that names no field on the object, with rule `autonumber-references-unknown-field`. It is a gating authoring rule for every CLI command and the runtime publish gate.
  - The card's `24Q-001` is the bare renderer's answer.
- **Every format the page keeps renders what its comment says:**
  - `{0000}` → `0001`
  - `{YYYY}-{0000}` → `2024-0001`
  - `{YY}{MM}-{000}` → `2403-001`
  - `ORD-{YYYYMMDD}-{00}` → `ORD-20240315-01`
  - `PO-{YYYY}-{MM}-{0000}` → `PO-2024-03-0001`
  - `INV-{0000}` → `INV-0001`
- **Counter scope.** `ORD-{YYYY}-{0000}` renders scope `ORD-2024-`, and `ORD-{0000}` renders an empty scope. The spec's `FieldSchema` doc for `autonumberFormat` says the same: "The counter is scoped to whatever renders BEFORE the `{0000}` slot, so the period/group resets fall out automatically — no separate reset config".
- **Exports.** `parseAutonumberFormat` and `renderAutonumber` are functions on `@objectstack/spec/data`. Neither is on the root `@objectstack/spec` entry (both read `undefined` there), so the page names the subpath.

## Triage's third bullet (teach `autonumberFormat`): measured, and not done here

Triage asked the page to teach `autonumberFormat`, which the spec prefers for a new field. The page's typed literals use `AutoNumberFieldMetadata` (`@object-ui/types`). That type declares `format` and does not declare `autonumberFormat`, and `check:doc-snippets` compiles this page's `ts` fences (the page is not in its `UNGATED_DOCS`).

I tested this with a one-off mutation. The fix was committed first, and objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` did the swap and the restore:

- **Mutation.** The page's `invoiceNumber` literal changed from `format: 'INV-{0000}'` to `autonumberFormat: 'INV-{0000}'`. The anchor hit once, the blob moved, and the gate went red: `TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'autonumberFormat' does not exist in type 'AutoNumberFieldMetadata'.` (788 of 788 blocks judged, 1 failed).
- **Restore.** The blob equals HEAD and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

Teaching the key would need `AutoNumberFieldMetadata` to declare it. That is a widening and a card of its own, and the dev report hands it to the seat. So the typed literals stay on `format`, which the spec also accepts. The page does not mention `autonumberFormat`, so it teaches no key that its own authoring type refuses.

## Bounded in-place repair: the Sequence Management sentence

The new Backend Implementation text says the backend renders with the spec's renderer. The old sentence in the next section said the per-year counter was optional ("if the sequence is meant to restart each January"), which contradicts that renderer: its scope is the rendered prefix, so a `{YYYY}` before the slot always restarts the count. All four exemption conditions hold:

1. **Same defect class as this card.** The page teaches format semantics the spec's renderer does not have.
2. **Mechanical, with a pinned shape.** The spec doc quoted above states the rule, and the scopes were measured.
3. **No other claim holds the file.** The claim's file surface is this one file.
4. **Same gate family.** It adds no new verification surface.

The diff changes no file ESLint reads.

Landing note: the `Type Check` red on package-less diffs that objectui#12272 described is addressed by PR objectui#12277, which landed as `48fb558d`. This branch's base is that commit.

## Acceptance notes

- One `{Q}` remains on the page, on purpose. It is in the new warning sentence ("`{Q}` reads a field called `Q`, not the quarter"), which tells a reader, or an agent, why no quarter token exists.
- I did not use the card's wording "the page's own example renders `24Q-001`". That is the bare renderer's answer. Through a real object, the format is a compile-time refusal or an insert-time throw, as measured above.
- The three `SchemaExample` sources write `"type": "auto_number"` inside a form's `fields`. That is the form's widget key, per `AutoNumberFieldMetadata`'s own doc comment, so it is not a contradiction of the page's `autonumber` sentence. I did not touch them, because they are outside the claim's file surface.
